top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock is a new measurement principle (magic-wavelength cancellation of light shifts, so many atoms are interrogated free of Doppler and recoil shifts), not only a better number, and it is distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 single-quantum-system prizes. Independent clocks at JILA, RIKEN/Tokyo, PTB, NIST and SYRTE agree at 10^-18, and the clocks already act as instruments on nature (millimetre-scale gravitational redshift, limits on drifting constants and dark matter). The Katori and Ye allocation is clean and the citation scope is narrow and defensible; no award is the only alternative on the slate and would withhold a mature, verified discovery.
